name: ocr-worker

bundle.note: FL-9's GUARD, and this member is the first one it did not already fit. The two `external` entries are not npm packages: they are the member's own UPLOAD PARTS, declared so the guard's one-part-resolution check knows what an installer must ship beside the bundle rather than reporting them as unresolvable. `assets` is the other half — CPDF-10's additive arm in bio-plane/scripts/fleet-bundle.mjs hashes those files into the committed manifest, so a wasm core or a language model swapped underneath this member is STALENESS and FAILS, exactly as a changed source is. That matters more here than for either sibling: the engine's measured fidelity (CPDF-15, MEASUREMENTS.md 2026-09-10) is a fidelity OF THOSE EXACT BYTES, and the provenance chain this member produces names a `cap` that rests on it. TWO of this member's build inputs are other trees' — ../pdf-worker/src/pagepixels.mjs (CPDF-12's renderer) and ../bio-plane/src/pdfstructure.mjs behind it — so a change in either STALES this artifact, which is the cross-tree arm FL-9 already drives for pdf-worker.

note: The fleet-coverage marker (D-117). scripts/coverage.mjs discovers a fleet member by this file, reads its `surface` table from `entry`, and holds it to the same surfaces the plane is held to: each surface op reached by a suite in `testDir`, a declared negative control, and fleet rule 2 (no surface op may declare `mutating: true` — a member ASSERTS nothing). scripts/battery.mjs discovers members by this file too and RUNS their suites. This member has NO runtime dependency — tesseract-wasm is a devDependency used only to REGENERATE src/tesslib.mjs — so its suites run and its byte-identity arm is runnable on a checkout with no install here at all, which is deliberate: a guard that skips is not a guard.
